_comment: Citations for what an ANALYSIS run invokes, beside install/references.bib which covers the
pipeline's own tools. Same shape, same compiler: this file is the one to edit, it compiles
to citations.json beside it with dev/scripts/bib2citations.py, and bin/write_citations.py
turns the merged set into CITATIONS.md and references.bib inside every published folder.
Three sources are merged for one analysis. PoolSeqFlow and Nextflow come from
install/, so there is one copy of each in the release. This file adds what the analysis
layer itself runs on. A module adds its own methods citations in its own references.bib,
because a module is published separately and the frame cannot hold a list of citations for
modules that do not exist yet.
There is no 'when' gate here: what a run invoked is decided before the writer is called,
by merging only the module that actually ran. An entry that is in the merged set is one
'r_package' names the R package an entry is about, and the version reported is the one
R answers with rather than the one the environment pins.
GENERATED from references.bib beside this file. Do not edit it: dev/scripts/bib2citations.py overwrites it, and 00_static fails when the two differ.

hivert2018.name: Effective sample size for Pool-seq
hivert2018.authors: Hivert, Valentin and Leblois, Rapha{\"e}l and Petit, Eric J. and Gautier, Mathieu and Vitalis, Renaud
hivert2018.title: Measuring Genetic Differentiation from Pool-seq Data
hivert2018.note: The effective sample size the analysis layer weights by, n_eff = n*d / (n + d - 1) for a pool of n chromosomes read to depth d. The paper does not write it in that form - it defines D2 as the sum of (d + n - 1)/n, which is the sum of d / n_eff under this form and under no other. Its pools are parameterized by HAPLOID size, which is what leaves n_eff, and everything weighted by it, general over ploidy. It is HERE rather than in a module because analysis/lib/R/n_eff.R is library code and every module that weights anything calls it.

nei1972.name: Nei's minimum genetic distance
nei1972.title: Genetic Distance between Populations
nei1972.note: The distance the analysis layer places pools by, D_m = (J_X + J_Y)/2 - J_XY, where J is the probability that two chromosomes carry the same allele. It is the MINIMUM distance of this paper and not the standard distance D, which is defined in the same one and is a log of a ratio; the minimum distance is linear in the J terms, so averaging over loci and averaging over sites are the same operation and no ratio-of-averages question arises. What is applied here beyond the paper is the sampling correction: each J is replaced by its unbiased estimator from a sample of n_eff chromosomes, and J_XY takes none because the two pools are sequenced independently. It is HERE rather than in a module because analysis/lib/R/nei_distance.R is library code.

ggplot2.title: ggplot2: Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis
